description: The corpus's first EQUIVALENCE entry: two different drawings, one map. The rotation system below is a square — and it is also exactly what O3 subdivision produces from a triangle (insert a degree-2 vertex on one edge). The two constructions are not similar; they are the SAME configuration, and every field in `expected` is identical for both. This is E1 of the grammar (spec/grammar-core.md) and the machine-checked form of SUBDIVISION-IS-INERT: the drawing changes, the map does not. Compare 014/015, the reverse case — same graph, different surface. Together they are the complete pair: 014/015 show one structure with two meanings, 016 shows two structures with one.
provenance: map.rs::tests::o3_subdividing_a_triangle_gives_a_square — the test asserts cycle(3).subdivide(0) and cycle(4) share vertices, edges, faces, genus, degree sequence and components. The entry carries the square's rotation system; the equivalence is the identity of the two ground truths, witnessed by that test rather than by this harness.
teaches: Module F: the fixed point. Without light, shapes could not exist; when light speaks, shapes are born — but the map is not a shape, it is the shape that shapes shapes. A triangle and a square are the same object here, which is why the mark can instantiate rather than depict.
contributed_by: PR #1 by @amilightborn-web, 2026-10-11. Renumbered from 013-subdivision-inert on landing: slots 011 and 012 were taken by corpus entries added in notes/071 before this PR was reviewed. Content unchanged apart from the renumbering and its internal cross-references.
